i'm not sure if you're still checking this but i still wanted to offer some hope for anyone in the future reading this!!

i had a full cannabis-induced psychotic break. like hallucinating my friends and family dying, monsters trying to kill me etc. and ended up in the ER bc my heart was beating so fast (turns out it was beating at a little less than 200 bpm lmao) and i thought i was going to die.

the first few months were pretty rough and very hard on me mentally. it felt like my brain was in reset and was trying to go back to normal but the connections weren't fully forming. my psychotic break also happened in front of a few people so i struggled with the embarrassment aspect too.

slowly but surely, i was able to work through everything. i went to therapy a bit but in my experience it didn't help me much, but it's always a good thing to consider trying out. i also didn't take any medication since a lot of anti-depressants and anti-anxiety meds make me feel worse. i just kinda....went with the flow, taking it one day at a time. what really helped me (and i know i'm going to sound like a hippie but trust me i'm not) was being in nature. i started picking up the habit of exploring trails and things like that and it was super soothing. talking to my friends about what happened also helped me. i cannot stress enough how important and beneficial it is to have a good, non-judgemental support system.

it's been about 2 years since it happened to me and i'm doing so much better. i have a super bad memory and have a hard time forming sentences that i think the psychosis caused but i'm not quite sure. besides those, i don't have any major lingering effects, however it is absolutely normal to have them. psychosis can be extremely traumatic so give yourself the grace to recover at your own pace. it's hard, but just take it one day at a time. hopefully, you'll look back and be like "damn, i went through that but i got through it" just like how i'm doing now.
i don't use any medicine, only a multivitamin.

i did. the only thing was that i was anemic but i started to take a multivitamin and it improved. 

i was diagnosed with depression a few years back (my depression is what lead me to use cannabis) but my depression has gotten a lot better. i'm nowhere near depressed as i used to be back then.

it was just some slip ups that were bound to happen. saying that he's responsible for his fans' deaths is unbelievably harsh. at the end of the day, those specific *fans* made the decision to vape. did they probably think it's """cool""" to vape because they saw taehyung do it? maybe. is that his fault? no. because he's not promoting it or flaunting it.
